items.title: Section: The Chapter of Deciding Discernment Opens — Why the Buddha Kept the Store-Consciousness a Secret

items.zh: 如是已說本地。次說諸地決擇善巧。由此決擇善巧為依、於一切地善能問答。今當先說五識身地、意地決擇。問：前說種子依，謂阿賴耶識。而未說有、有之因緣、廣分別義。何故不說？何緣知有？廣分別義云何應知？答：由此建立是佛世尊最深密記，是故不說。
items.en:
Within the Chapter of Deciding Discernment, the Five Sense-Consciousness-Corresponding Ground and the Mind Ground, part one.
Second major division, the Chapter of Deciding Discernment; first, concluding what precedes and generating what follows. The basic stages having thus been fully explained, next comes the skilful discernment deciding the deeper meaning of every stage. Relying on this skilful discernment, one becomes capable of skilfully answering any question concerning any stage.
Second, deciding everything; first, the Five Sense-Consciousness-Corresponding Ground and the Mind Ground; first, stating what should be said first. Now, first, the discernment of the Five Sense-Consciousness-Corresponding Ground and the Mind Ground shall be explained.
Second, deciding what corresponds, in five parts; first, the store-consciousness; first, the question. Question: it was previously said that the basis of seeds is called the store-consciousness, yet its existence, the reasoning for its existence, and its full, detailed meaning were not explained. Why was it not explained? By what reasoning is its existence known? How should its full, detailed meaning be understood?
Second, the answer; first, the reason it was not explained; first, stating the meaning. Answer: because this establishment is the Blessed One's own most profound, secret record, it was therefore not explained.

items.title: Section: "Deep and Subtle Flows the Store of Every Seed" — The Celebrated Ādāna Verse

items.zh: 如世尊言：阿陀那識甚深細，一切種子如瀑流。我於凡、愚不開演，恐彼分別執為我。
items.en: Second, citing proof. As the Blessed One said: the ādāna-consciousness is deep and subtle, every seed within it like a raging torrent; I do not reveal it to the ordinary and the foolish, fearing they would discriminate and cling to it as a self.

items.title: Section: Eight Arguments Named in Verse — Why Ordinary Consciousness Alone Cannot Explain a Living Body

items.zh: 復次，嗢拕南曰：執受、初、明了、種子、業、身受、無心定、命終，無，皆不應理。由八種相，證阿賴耶識決定是有。謂若離阿賴耶識，依止執受不應道理，最初生起不應道理，有明了性不應道理，有種子性不應道理，業用差別不應道理，身受差別不應道理，處無心定不應道理，命終時識不應道理。
items.en:
Second, the reasoning for its existence; first, presenting all eight characteristics together; first, the summary verse. Furthermore, the summary verse states: appropriation, the first arising, clarity of cognition, having the nature of seeds, function, bodily sensation, mindless concentration, and consciousness at death — without it, none of these would make sense.
Second, the prose. Through eight characteristics, the store-consciousness is definitively proven to exist. That is, apart from the store-consciousness: the basis of appropriation makes no sense; the very first arising makes no sense; the presence of clarity in cognition makes no sense; the nature of holding seeds makes no sense; differences in function make no sense; differences in bodily sensation make no sense; abiding in mindless concentration makes no sense; and consciousness at the moment of death makes no sense.

items.title: Section: The First Proof Begins — Three Reasons Why Only the Store-Consciousness Can Sustain a Living Body

items.zh: 何故若無阿賴耶識，依止執受不應道理？由五因故。何等為五？謂阿賴耶識先世所造業行為因，眼等轉識於現在世眾緣為因。如說根及境界、作意力故，諸轉識生，乃至廣說。是名初因。又六識身，有善不善等性可得。是第二因。又六識身，無覆無記異熟所攝類不可得。是第三因。
items.en:
Second, explaining each individually; first, appropriation; first, posing the question. Why, apart from the store-consciousness, does the basis of appropriation make no sense?
Second, explaining; first, stating. For five reasons.
Second, posing the question. What are these five?
Third, explaining; first, the first reason. The store-consciousness has past karmic action as its cause, while the eye-consciousness and other active consciousnesses have the present coming together of conditions as their cause. As it is said, consciousness arises through the coming together of a sense faculty, an object, and attention, and so on at length. This is the first reason.
Second, the second reason. The six active consciousnesses can be found possessing wholesome, unwholesome, and other natures. This is the second reason.
Third, the third reason. The six active consciousnesses cannot be found belonging to the category of morally neutral, fully ripened consciousness. This is the third reason.

items.zh: 又六識身各別依轉。於彼彼依，彼彼識轉，即彼所依應

items.title: Section: Two Final Reasons — Why an Eye-Consciousness Cannot Sustain an Ear, and the First Proof Closes

items.zh: 有執受，餘無執受不應道理。設許執受，亦不應理。識遠離故。是第四因。又所依止應成數數執受過失。所以者何？由彼眼識於一時轉，一時不轉，餘識亦爾。是第五因。如是先業及現在緣以為因故，善不善等性可得故，異熟種類不可得故，各別所依諸識轉故，數數執受依止過故，不應道理。
items.en:
Second, challenging that appropriation could be present. Even granting appropriation this way, it still makes no sense, since consciousness is localised elsewhere.
Second, presenting the reason. This is the fourth reason.
Fifth, the fifth reason; first, showing the fault; first, stating. Also, the basis of appropriation would suffer the fault of being repeatedly appropriated and unappropriated.
Second, posing the question. Why is this?
Third, explaining. Because the eye-consciousness arises at one time and fails to arise at another, and likewise for the other consciousnesses.
Second, presenting the reason. This is the fifth reason.
Third, concluding. Thus, because of having past karma and present conditions as their respective causes, because wholesome, unwholesome, and other natures can be found, because the category of ripened consciousness cannot be found, because each active consciousness arises in dependence on its own separate faculty, and because the fault of repeated appropriation would result — for these reasons, it does not make sense.

items.title: Section: Watching, Listening, Tasting, and Smelling All at Once — Proving That Consciousnesses Truly Co-Arise

items.zh: 何故若無阿賴耶識，最初生起不應道理？謂有難言：若決定有阿賴耶識，應有二識俱時生起。應告彼言：汝於無過妄生過想，何以故？容有二識俱時轉故。所以者何？且如有一，俱時欲見乃至欲知，隨有一識最初生起，不應道理。由彼爾時作意無別，根、境亦爾；以何因緣識不俱轉？
items.en:
Second, a first-arising consciousness; first, posing the question. Why, apart from the store-consciousness, does the notion of a first-arising consciousness fail to make sense?
Second, explaining; first, presenting the objection. It is objected: if the store-consciousness definitely existed, two consciousnesses would have to arise simultaneously.
Second, refuting this as mistaken; first, stating that co-arising is possible. One should reply: you raise a false objection where there is no actual fault. Why? Because it is entirely possible for two consciousnesses to arise together at once.
Second, explaining why; first, refuting the mistaken view. Why is this? Suppose a person simultaneously wishes to see and so on up through wishing to cognize; claiming that, in such a case, only a single consciousness arises first makes no sense at all.
Second, revealing the correct view. Because attention at that moment is undivided, and the faculty and object are likewise undivided, by what reasoning would the consciousnesses fail to operate together?

items.title: Section: Why Recalling the Past Feels Hazy But Perceiving the Present Feels Sharp — The Third Proof Begins

items.zh: 何故若無諸識俱轉，與眼等識同行意識明了體性不可得耶？謂或有時憶念過去曾所受境，爾時意識行不明了；非於現境意現行時，得有如是不明了相。是故應許諸識俱轉。或許意識無明了性。
items.en:
Third, clarity of cognition; first, posing the question. Why, if consciousnesses did not co-arise, would the mental consciousness accompanying the eye-consciousness and the rest fail to possess its own characteristic clarity?
Second, explaining; first, establishing that consciousnesses co-arise. Sometimes, recollecting a past object once experienced, the mental consciousness's activity in that moment is unclear; but when the mental consciousness engages a present object, no such unclear characteristic is ever found. Therefore one should grant that consciousnesses co-arise.
Second, challenging the absence of clarity. Or else one must concede that the mental consciousness lacks clarity even then.

items.title: Section: The Fourth Proof — Why Ever-Shifting Consciousness Cannot Hold Seeds the Way a Stable One Can

items.zh: 何故若無阿賴耶識，有種子性不應道理？謂六識身展轉異故。所以者何？從善無間不善性生，不善無間復善性生，從二無間無記性生；劣界無間中界生，中界無間妙界生，如是妙界無間乃至劣界生；有漏無間無漏生，無漏無間有漏生；世間無間出世生，出世無間世間生；非如是相有種子性，應正道理。又彼諸識長時間斷，不應相續長時流轉，是故此亦不應道理。
items.en:
Fourth, the nature of holding seeds; first, posing the question. Why, apart from the store-consciousness, does having the nature of holding seeds fail to make sense?
Second, explaining; first, through transformation; first, stating. Because the six active consciousnesses continually shift and become other than they were.
Second, posing the question. Why is this?
Third, explaining. A wholesome state gives way immediately to an unwholesome one, an unwholesome state gives way to a wholesome one, and both give way to a neutral state; the inferior realm gives way to the middling realm, the middling gives way to the exquisite, and the exquisite gives way back to the inferior; the contaminated gives way to the uncontaminated, and the uncontaminated gives way back to the contaminated; the mundane gives way to the transmundane, and the transmundane gives way back to the mundane. Such being the case, having the nature of holding seeds does not make sense.
Second, through interruption. Also, these consciousnesses undergo long periods of interruption, and so cannot sustain the long continuity required for seeds to carry across saṃsāra.

items.title: Section: Four Things Cognized in a Single Instant — World, Body, Self, and Object All at Once

items.zh: 何故若無諸識俱轉，業用差別不應道理？謂若略說有四種業。一、了別器業，二、了別依業，三、了別我業，四、了別境業。此諸了別，剎那剎那俱轉可得，是故一識於一剎那有如是等業用差別，不應道理。
items.en:
Fifth, differences in function; first, posing the question. Why, apart from consciousnesses co-arising, do differences in function fail to make sense?
Second, explaining; first, listing them. In brief, there are four kinds of function: cognizing the environment, cognizing the basis, cognizing a self, and cognizing an object.
Second, refuting the mistaken view. These acts of cognition are found occurring together moment after moment; therefore, claiming that a single consciousness in a single moment could perform such differing functions does not make sense.

blocks.text: Fascicle 51 opens the second great division of the treatise, the "Section on Ascertainment" (攝決擇分). It goes back over the seventeen stages and settles their difficult points. It begins with the most famous passage in Yogācāra: eight proofs that the store-consciousness (ālayavijñāna) must exist. From here the commentary draws mainly on Master Cháng Bǎi's lectures.

"Because this establishment is the Blessed One's own most profound, secret record, it was therefore not explained" in the earlier stages. Master Cháng Bǎi: a śrāvaka need only cut self-grasping to reach arhatship; but without understanding this consciousness, wisdom of all objects is hard to attain.

The verse (from the *Saṃdhinirmocana Sūtra*) says the ādāna-consciousness is deep and subtle, its seeds like a raging torrent, and that the Buddha did not teach it to the foolish lest they take it for a self. Master Cháng Bǎi: ādāna means "holding": it keeps seeds from being lost. It was not taught openly because it is subtle and continues as if one and constant; ordinary beings might cling to it as a self.
Master Cháng Bǎi: Yogācāra scholars hold that only with this consciousness can life be fully explained.
The six consciousnesses cannot be found as neutral, ripened consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: the physical faculties are the subtle sense organs, and the appropriated basis their physical supports.

subs.head: Only one can pervade the body

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: eye-consciousness does not arise at the ear, so how could it hold the ear? The store-consciousness pervades the whole body. (Untranslated, 0579b02: each of the six consciousnesses operates on its own separate basis.)
Attention, faculty, and object are all present. Master Cháng Bǎi: with conditions complete, several consciousnesses can function at once.
Recollection is unclear; present perception is clear. Master Cháng Bǎi: alone, the mental consciousness is unclear about the past; together with the five senses, it is clear.

The six keep changing and are often interrupted. Master Cháng Bǎi: good and evil exclude each other, so they cannot hold each other's seeds. In the heaven without perception, the six do not appear for nearly five hundred eons; who then holds past karmic seeds?
Cognising the environment, the body, a self, and an object. Master Cháng Bǎi: all four occur at once.
The argument is careful and empirical: we see and hear at the same moment; a long meditation ends and the mind returns with its memories. Something must hold it all together.

quiz.q: Why was the store-consciousness not explained in detail in the basic section?
options: because this establishment is the Blessed One's most profound, secret record
quiz.why: "Because this establishment is the Blessed One's own most profound, secret record, it was therefore not explained." Master Cháng Bǎi: from this chapter on, the essentials of consciousness-only are explained in detail.

quiz.q: Why does the Buddha not reveal it to the foolish, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: it is subtle, continuing as if one and constant; ordinary people would cling to it as a self
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the store-consciousness is subtle and continues as if one and constant; if taught, ordinary beings might cling to it as a self.

quiz.q: Can a śrāvaka attain arhatship without understanding the store-consciousness?
options: yes: cutting self-grasping suffices, but omniscient wisdom is then hard to reach
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a śrāvaka need only cut self-grasping to reach arhatship; but without understanding this consciousness, wisdom of all objects is hard to attain.

quiz.q: To what does the verse compare the seeds of the ādāna-consciousness?
quiz.why: Every seed is like a raging torrent. Master Cháng Bǎi: with regard to seeds it is "holding" — the ādāna-consciousness keeps seeds from being lost.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish "subtle" from "very deep and subtle"?
options: subtle excludes ordinary people; very subtle addresses the two vehicles
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "subtle" sets it apart from ordinary people's coarse understanding; "very subtle" addresses the two vehicles, who have already broken self-grasping.

quiz.q: Through how many characteristics is its existence proven?
quiz.why: Eight. Master Cháng Bǎi: consciousness-only scholars hold that only with this consciousness can life be fully explained.

quiz.q: What is the third reason regarding appropriation?
options: the six cannot be found in the category of neutral ripened consciousness
quiz.why: The six cannot be found as neutral ripened consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: they arise from ripened seeds, but aren't true ripening.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the fourth reason?
options: each depends on its own faculty; eye-consciousness can't appropriate the ear; only the store-consciousness pervades the body
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: eye-consciousness doesn't arise at the ear, so how could it appropriate the ear? The store-consciousness pervades the whole body.

quiz.q: "The very first arising." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say this concerns?
options: the śrāvaka view of serial arising; not life's beginning, nor the sequence of the links
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the śrāvaka holds that consciousnesses arise serially, hence a "first" one; this is not the sequence of the links. "Very first" can mislead.

options: attention is undivided, and so are faculty and object; nothing prevents co-arising
quiz.why: Attention, faculty, and object are all present. Master Cháng Bǎi: with conditions complete, they can function at once.

quiz.q: What phenomenon establishes that consciousnesses co-arise?
options: recollection is unclear, while engaging a present object isn't
quiz.why: Recollection is unclear, present engagement clear. Master Cháng Bǎi: alone, the mental consciousness is unclear about the past; with the five, it is clear.

quiz.q: Why can't the six hold seeds? Which two reasons are given?
options: they keep changing, and are interrupted for long periods
quiz.why: They keep changing and are long interrupted. Master Cháng Bǎi: good and evil exclude each other, so they can't hold each other's seeds.

options: cognizing the environment, basis, self, and object
quiz.why: Cognizing environment, basis, self, and object. Master Cháng Bǎi: all four occur at once.
